record.original_question: Can one identify abstract classes of variational objectives on probability measures and corresponding random approximations such that the objective values E(mu_n) converge to E(mu_*) as the number of samples grows, quantitative convergence rates can be proved under explicit model assumptions, and the resulting abstract classes still cover problems of practical interest in machine learning?

evidence.quote: Our vision leads to the following theoretical problem: Can we define abstract classes of objectives E and of their (random) approximations En , such that E(µn ) converges to E(µ∗ ) as n goes to infinity? Can we give rates of convergence of such a convergence under some well-specified model assumptions? Do those abstract classes describe problems of practical interest?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ denote the set of Borel probability measures on a Polish space $\mathcal{X}$. Consider a variational objective $E:\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ and, for each integer $n\ge 1$, a random empirical-style approximation $E_n:\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ built from $n$ i.i.d. samples (or analogous random data) drawn from an underlying data distribution. Let
$$\mu_* \in \arg\min_{\mu\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} E(\mu), \qquad \mu_n \in \arg\min_{\mu\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} E_n(\mu).$$

The problem is to identify abstract classes $\mathcal{C}$ of pairs $(E,(E_n)_{n\ge 1})$ such that all three of the following hold:

(i) (Consistency) For every $(E,(E_n))\in\mathcal{C}$, one has $E(\mu_n)\to E(\mu_*)$ as $n\to\infty$, in probability or almost surely.

(ii) (Quantitative rates) There exist explicit model assumptions on $(E,(E_n))$ (e.g., regularity, convexity, concentration, dimension, smoothness of densities) under which one can prove non-asymptotic bounds of the form $\mathbb{E}[E(\mu_n)-E(\mu_*)] \le r(n)$ with an explicit rate function $r(n)\to 0$.

(iii) (Practical scope) The class $\mathcal{C}$ is broad enough to encompass variational objectives on measures arising in machine learning practice, such as those used for out-of-distribution generalization, weakly supervised learning, or uncertainty quantification.

Provide such classes $\mathcal{C}$, together with proofs of (i)–(ii) and a demonstration of (iii).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as an open problem in a 2023 vision/open-problem note by Cabannes and Domingo-Enrich. No subsequent work appears to provide a comprehensive abstract framework simultaneously satisfying consistency, explicit rates, and broad coverage of practical ML measure-valued objectives; related contemporaneous works (e.g., convergence of coordinate-ascent variational inference, accelerated optimization over measure spaces) address particular instances rather than the general abstract program. Status remains open.

status_evidence.title: Convergence of coordinate ascent variational inference for log-concave measures
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence results for CAVI in the log-concave case via optimal transport.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses specific variational settings rather than the general abstract program.

status_evidence.title: Accelerating optimization over the space of probability measures
status_evidence.snippet: Accelerated optimization methods on Wasserstein space.
status_evidence.claim: Related work focuses on optimization rather than statistical consistency/rates for empirical approximations of measure-valued objectives in general.
